source_patches.why: libgcc's 64-bit divide/modulo (func_001A0660/0CF8/1388/1908, used by the duel's angle maths): umul_ppmm is a MIPS multu asm statement, which the generator turns into 0, so a divisor above 32 bits gave a wrong quotient; the same 32x32->64 multiply in C

Ta_ConvBitLengthToNumericLength (the AI's n-bit masks, Ta_* in main_072): the asm sums pow(2.0, i) for i < n in the EE's software doubles (func_001A2EB0 int->double, func_001A6BE8 -> pow, func_001A2858 add, func_001A2F68 double->int), so it returns 2^n - 1. The decomp's soft-double calls typed as ints came out as func_001A2F68(0) (always 0) and pow called through an int cast, which left one x87 register pushed per call: after 8 calls every float result in the program was NaN (lane G's oracle, seed 2). Same sum in plain C
